model_fitness.best_available_model: Tsc2 hypomorphic mouse with spontaneous, translationally relevant seizures (PMID:37545094), cross-checked in Tsc1-GFAP conditional knockout and neuronal Tsc1-KO mice (PMID:37399505)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the core mechanism: biallelic Tsc loss drives constitutive mTORC1 with elevated pS6 and p4E-BP1 in brain, and the readouts needed (regional p4E-BP1 as the rapamycin-resistant output, pAKT-S473 as the mTORC2 output) are directly measurable in the same tissue that generates the seizures. EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:37399505; PMID:37545094.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partial. Astrocytes, neurons and neural progenitors carrying Tsc loss are represented, and the Tsc1-GFAP CKO gives a glial-driven epilepsy phenotype. No mouse reproduces human cortical tubers with giant cells or the laminar disorganization of human perituberal cortex, so target engagement in 'tuber tissue' is modelled only by proxy. INFERENCE, inconclusive.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Continuous video-EEG seizure frequency and burden, plus survival, with paired pharmacodynamics (cortical and perituberal-equivalent pS6, p4E-BP1, pAKT-S473) and free (unbound) brain and plasma drug concentrations. This is the exact pairing the decision needs: did we normalize the rapamycin-resistant output, and did seizures follow?
model_fitness.important_limitations: Mouse seizures do not predict human seizure response quantitatively; germline biallelic models have more uniform and more severe mTOR activation than the mosaic two-hit human lesion, which may make deep inhibition look better than it will be in patients. Mouse P-gp handling differs from human, so free-brain-fraction translation is approximate. No model addresses chronic paediatric tolerability of TORC1/2 blockade, which is the programme's real failure mode. The available catalytic compounds are tool compounds with genotoxicity and primate tolerability liabilities, so a positive result licenses a discovery programme, not a candidate. EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37399505.

plan.critical_question: Do residual seizures on maximal allosteric mTORC1 inhibition reflect insufficient brain target engagement (specifically, persistent rapamycin-resistant 4E-BP1 phosphorylation), or fixed circuit pathology that deeper mTOR kinase inhibition cannot reach? Everything downstream - whether to fund multi-year CNS-optimized chemistry - depends on this single answer.
plan.proposed_experiment: Head-to-head, pharmacodynamically anchored seizure study. In the Tsc2 hypomorphic spontaneous-seizure model (PMID:37545094), with the Tsc1-GFAP CKO as a second genotype, run three arms plus vehicle: (1) everolimus at a maximal chronically tolerated regimen; (2) a brain-penetrant ATP-competitive mTOR tool compound (TC1 or congener, PMID:37399505; PMID:37545094) dose-titrated in a pilot PK/PD cohort to the lowest dose that normalizes cortical p4E-BP1 to wild-type levels; (3) everolimus plus intermittent/pulsed catalytic dosing, to test whether mTORC2 sparing can be preserved. Treat from after seizure onset (the clinically relevant, hardest case). Primary: continuous video-EEG for 3-4 weeks (baseline and on-treatment). In parallel terminal cohorts at matched timepoints: regional immunoblot/immunohistochemistry for pS6-S235/236, p4E-BP1-T37/46 and pAKT-S473 in cortex, hippocampus and subependymal zone, with simultaneous unbound brain and plasma concentrations (brain homogenate binding / equilibrium dialysis). Power the EEG arms for a 50 percent between-arm difference in seizure frequency. Pre-register the PD acceptance criterion: an arm only counts as 'deep engagement achieved' if cortical p4E-BP1 is statistically indistinguishable from wild-type.
plan.model: Tsc2 hypomorphic mouse with spontaneous seizures (PMID:37545094), confirmed in Tsc1-GFAP conditional knockout; treatment initiated after seizure onset.
plan.primary_readout: Percent reduction in video-EEG seizure frequency and total seizure burden versus vehicle, interpreted strictly against the paired pharmacodynamic readout - cortical p4E-BP1 normalization - and free-brain drug concentration. Secondary: pAKT-S473 suppression as the mTORC2 toxicity surrogate, survival, and body weight/growth as a first tolerability signal.
plan.supportive_result: The catalytic arm normalizes cortical p4E-BP1 where everolimus does not, and this is accompanied by a substantially larger seizure reduction (for example seizure freedom or greater than 75 percent reduction versus roughly 30-40 percent for everolimus) in animals that are everolimus-refractory. This establishes that residual seizures are target-engagement-limited and that the differentiating pharmacology is real. Decision: proceed, but immediately to the window question, not to chemistry - run the chronic juvenile tolerability study of the pulsed/combination arm before committing to lead optimization.
plan.negative_result: Full normalization of cortical p4E-BP1 (confirmed by PD, not assumed from dose) produces no meaningful additional seizure reduction over maximally dosed everolimus, or improves seizures only at exposures that also abolish pAKT-S473 systemically and cause weight loss/overt toxicity. Either outcome refutes the premise: the first says the residual disease is fixed circuit pathology, the second says the mechanism cannot be separated from its toxicity. Decision: do not fund CNS-optimized catalytic mTOR chemistry for epilepsy; redirect to earlier/preventive treatment timing (pre-seizure-onset dosing, the stronger hypothesis given the 46 percent paediatric versus 14 percent adult response, PMID:38042867) or to mTOR-independent circuit targets.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to commit to a multi-year, de novo CNS-optimized ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor discovery programme. There is currently no de-risked chemical starting point - published brain-penetrant catalytic compounds carry in vitro genotoxicity, poor oral exposure in higher species and dose-limiting primate toxicity, and no clinical-stage agent was CNS-optimized (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37399505) - so the cost of being wrong is very high and the cost of this experiment is low. A negative result stops the programme for roughly the price of one mouse EEG study; a positive result redefines the programme as a therapeutic-window problem, where the pulsed/combination arm is the de-risking strategy rather than chronic full TORC1/2 blockade.
